scope: Theorem 3.2 (Reciprocal affine maps by shears) of the manuscript “Finite Instructions and Solenoidal Shear Flows” (preprints/Finite-Instructions-and-Solenoidal-Shear-Flows-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0cdc2abd5b1a3d15), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For 1 ≤ i ≤ N, let Pi, Qi be closed axis-parallel rectangles with rational endpoints and positive side lengths in the planar chart of T3 L. Let their centers be pi, qi, and suppose Fi(X) = qi + diag(λi, λ−1 i )(X − pi), Fi(Pi) = Qi, λi ∈ Q>0. Assume the following: (i) The Pi are pairwise positively separated, and the Qi are pairwise positively separated. (ii) Every coordinate half-width of every Pi and Qi is at most a given rational h > 0. (iii) All pi, qi belong to a closed rectangle K with rational endpoints, and K +[−2h, 2h]2 is compactly contained in the planar chart. (iv) The coding height z0 is rational and lies inside the vertical chart. There is an effectively constructed smooth velocity V on R × T3 L with the following properties. (a) It is one-periodic in time and vanishes near every integer time. Every mixed space and time derivative has an effective uniform bound. (b) div V = 0, R T3 L V = 0, and (V · ∇)V = 0. (c) Its period map is (X, z) 7→ (Fi(X), z) on an effectively specified positive neighborhood of each Pi × {z0}. (d) Starting from (X, z0) with X ∈ Pi, the four scaling stages stay within horizontal sup distance 2h of pi. The next stage follows ((1 − θ)pi + θqi) + d, where 0 ≤ θ ≤ 1 and |d|∞ ≤ h. The lifting and lowering stages leave X unchanged. (e) For each fixed positive computable ν, the force f = ∂tV − ν∆V is smooth, mean zero, and solenoidal, with period one and bounded mixed derivatives. Equation (1) from zero initial velocity has the solution (u, p) = (V, 0), with uniformly bounded kinetic energy. This solution is unique among spatially periodic classical solutions for which u, its spatial derivatives through order two, ut, p, and ∇p are continuous on each finite closed time cylinder, and p has zero spatial mean at each time. No separation between a source and a target is required. For N = 0 the zero velocity has all the asserted properties, with no branch conditions.
